One of the solutions—or at least mitigations—Apple has proposed to address the memory shortage is to source RAM from two Chinese companies, CXMT and YMTC.

While not technically prohibited, doing so would put Apple on a collision course with the US government, and the idea now looks even less viable due to two new developments…

As far back as June, we knew Apple was seeking Trump administration approval to source memory chips from China. Although there's no actual legal ban preventing it, a Pentagon blacklist means that iPhones using chips from these two companies could be partially or fully banned for federal employees. It would also expose the Cupertino company to significant political or PR risk.

We noted at the time that Apple seemed unlikely to get the approval it was seeking, and the latest reporting appears to drive yet another nail into the coffin of the idea.

First, while sourcing from these two Chinese companies isn't currently illegal, a New York Times report suggests that could soon change.

Second, even if things stay as they are, a Wall Street Journal report says CXMT simply can't fulfil Apple's orders.

I previously described this as an unlikely solution; now I'd say it's extremely unlikely.
